homebrew.name: core-cookbook
homebrew.title: Core+: The Cookbook
homebrew.credit: Original meals for The Scavenger's Codex.
homebrew.desc: 42 meals for a cook with cook's utensils, from campfire fry-ups and trail food to uncommon feasts.

items.name: Giant Boar Roast
items.effect: One serving takes an hour to eat. For the next 8 hours you have temporary hit points equal to your proficiency bonus.

recipe.lore: The heart is slow-roasted in the belly of the joint so its stubborn vigour bastes the meat — boar hunters swear they can take a tusk to the ribs the morning after.

items.name: Hunter's Jerky
items.effect: Keeps for a month and counts as a day's food. For 8 hours after eating it you have advantage on saves against exhaustion from forced marches or going without sleep.

recipe.lore: Dried strips of heart are layered among the ordinary meat — rangers say a beast's endurance lives in its heart, and a pinch of wakeberry keeps the eyelids up.

items.name: Ranger's Trail Bread
items.effect: Dense, honeyed and nearly unspoilable. If you eat a slice during a short rest, you regain 1 extra hit point for each Hit Die you spend.

recipe.lore: Baked hard enough to break teeth, the bread is soaked in a stream before eating. Silverleaf or a crumb of manna in the dough is why it heals as it fills.

meal.lasts: until your next short or long rest

items.name: Seafarer's Chowder
items.effect: For 8 hours you can hold your breath three times as long as normal and have advantage on checks to swim in rough water.

recipe.lore: Pearl divers' grandmothers simmer a dried sea horse or a swim bladder into the pot, and the kelp's air-pods make the broth fizz on the tongue.

items.name: Nightwatch Broth
items.effect: For 8 hours you have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight in dim light, and you can't be surprised while on watch if you are awake.

recipe.lore: Soldiers of the night watch have always sworn by owl-eye broth. Gloomsight mushrooms do the same job for the squeamish.

items.name: Lionsmane Honey Cakes
items.effect: For 1 hour after eating one, you have advantage on saving throws against being frightened.

recipe.lore: Squires eat them before their first battle. The thistle version is golden and sweet; the lion's-heart version is darker and, reputedly, braver.

items.name: Owlbear Stew
items.effect: A thick, feathery-smelling stew. For 8 hours you have advantage on Strength (Athletics) checks and count as one size larger for carrying and grappling.

recipe.lore: Owlbear eggs are cracked into the stew at the last moment and stirred until they thicken it. Mothers are advised to be several miles away first.

items.name: Smokehouse Hunter's Jerky
items.effect: Thin strips of game meat, salted and smoked over green hardwood until they bend without breaking. A bundle counts as one day of rations and keeps for a full season even in damp packs.

recipe.lore: Every hunting lodge has a smoke-rack and an argument about which meat jerks best; the answer is always whatever you killed yesterday, cut thin and salted hard.

items.name: Titanroast Feast
items.effect: A slow-roasted haunch of a huge beast, glazed around the still-warm heart of a great charger or stag. Up to six creatures who share it within an hour gain 2 temporary hit points and advantage on the next saving throw they make against exhaustion within 8 hours.

recipe.lore: Frontier cooks swear the heart of an animal that ran until it dropped carries its stubbornness into the roast; the giant meat is simply there so everyone gets a slab.

items.name: Brinepot Chowder
items.effect: A thick fisherman's stew of whatever the nets and harpoons brought in. A bowl counts as a meal, and a diver who eats it warm has advantage on the next Constitution check to resist exhaustion from cold water that day.

recipe.lore: Tentacle meat is too tough to eat on its own, so harbour cooks boil it with shark and crab until the whole pot turns gluey and warming.

items.name: Bogman's Pepperpot
items.effect: A peppery marsh stew thick with reptile and amphibian meat. Eaters have advantage on saving throws against disease caught from swamp water for the next 8 hours, thanks to the fierce peppers more than the meat.

recipe.lore: Swamp folk learned long ago that anything scaly or slimy is safe to eat once it's drowned in pepper and vinegar, and that the same brew keeps bog-fever away.

items.name: Crawler's Protein Cake
items.effect: Dense, nutty-tasting cakes pressed from insect larvae and the pale meat of giant arthropods. One cake counts as a full day's food and weighs only a quarter pound.

recipe.lore: Underdark traders and desert caravans both prize bug-meal for its weight; honey binds the crumbly paste into cakes that survive a month in a saddlebag.

items.name: Frostmarch Pemmican
items.effect: Pounded dried meat mixed with rendered fat and berries into dense bricks. A creature that eats one each day has advantage on saving throws against exhaustion from extreme cold.

recipe.lore: Beasts that survive the tundra carry their warmth as fat; pound that fat into lean meat and a traveller carries a little of the beast's winter coat in their belly.

items.name: Warheart Oat-Mash
items.effect: A warm mash of oats and powdered heart fed to a mount before battle. For 8 hours the animal's walking speed increases by 10 feet and it has advantage on saving throws against being frightened.

recipe.lore: Cavalry grooms dry the heart of a warhorse that died charging and grate a pinch into each feed; horses, they say, remember the courage of their own kind.

items.name: Heather-and-Honey Hillside Tea
items.effect: A dozen twists of dried heather, honeycomb and marshmallow root that brew into a sweet, throat-soothing tea. A cup during a short rest gives advantage on your next Constitution check or save against a cough, chill or ordinary cold-weather illness.

recipe.lore: Shepherds swear by it: heather for warmth, honey to carry it, and marshmallow root to coat a raw throat after a night on the fells.

items.name: Samphire Sailor's Pickle
items.effect: A crock of briny samphire and sea lettuce that keeps for months. A week of it alongside ordinary rations prevents scurvy and the slow sickness of long voyages, and it counts as a day's food per jar.

recipe.lore: Tidal-flat greens are the old deckhand's cure; salt and vinegar keep them crisp long after the coast is out of sight.

items.name: Drover's Hand Pies
items.effect: Crimped lard pastry around chopped, long-stewed meat and pot-herbs. A pie counts as a day's food and survives a week in a saddlebag; a traveller who shares a round of them by a strange inn's hearth gains +1 on Charisma (Persuasion) checks with the locals for the next hour.

recipe.lore: Every market-town tavern has its own crimp on the pastry edge, and old drovers can name the inn from the first bite.

items.name: Cattail Frog-Leg Fritters
items.effect: Frog legs dredged in pounded cattail-root flour and fried crisp in fat steeped with bog myrtle. A plate counts as a meal, and for 8 hours the resinous myrtle sweating from your skin keeps midges, mosquitoes and leeches off you, so a night in a marsh camp costs you no rest to biting insects.

recipe.lore: Marsh cooks dry the cattail roots on the boat's thwarts all morning, and the myrtle goes into the fat, never the batter, or the fritters taste of soap.

items.name: Venison and Wild Garlic Skewers
items.effect: Chunks of forest game threaded on green sticks between cloves of wild garlic and yarrow leaves, then charred over coals. A skewer counts as a meal, and if you eat it at breakfast you gain +1 on the next Constitution saving throw you make against disease before nightfall.

recipe.lore: Woodwardens leave the meat in a garlic-and-yarrow rub while camp is struck, and say no fever ever caught a man who smelled that strongly of breakfast.

items.name: Caravan Ash-Flatbread

meal.lasts: until the end of the day

items.effect: Unleavened rounds kneaded with camel-hump fat, buried in hot sand under the coals and brushed with aloe pulp. A round counts as a day's food and stays soft for a week; the first time you make a Constitution saving throw against extreme heat on the day you eat one, you have advantage on it.

recipe.lore: Caravan masters judge a new cook by the flatbread alone: it should crack like a shell and steam like a kettle when torn.

items.name: Deepway Tentacle Rings
items.effect: Rubbery tentacle sliced into rings, crusted in salted grain-flour and fried hard, then strung on a cord. A string counts as a day's food and keeps for a week, and gnawing them through a long watch keeps you sharp: for 1 hour after eating you have +1 on Wisdom (Perception) checks.

recipe.lore: Underdark traders beat the tentacle against a flat stone until it stops twitching; skip that step and the rings curl back into hooks in the pan.

items.name: Shepherd's Willow-Bark Goat Stew
items.effect: A thin, bitter-sweet mountain stew of goat, heather tips and a strip of willow bark that eases knees after a day of climbing. A bowl counts as a meal, and before your next long rest, when you roll a 1 on a Hit Die during a short rest, you can reroll it once.

recipe.lore: Highland shepherds fish the willow bark out before serving, and count it a poor stew if the bark comes out still curled.

items.name: Saltmarsh Crab Cakes
items.effect: Picked crab bound with meal and chopped samphire and fried in a hot skillet, a dockside breakfast. A cake counts as a meal, and for the next hour you gain +1 on Strength (Athletics) checks to row, haul nets or ropes, or swim.

recipe.lore: Fishwives on the strand keep the samphire raw and add it last, so each cake still squeaks of the sea when you bite it.

items.name: Wakeberry-Glazed Drumsticks
items.effect: Huge drumsticks from a big flightless or winged beast, glazed with crushed wakeberries and honey and roasted until the skin cracks. One feeds a hungry adult for the day, and the tart berries leave you twitchy-alert: for 1 hour you gain +1 on initiative rolls.

recipe.lore: Plains riders baste the drumsticks with a feather from the same bird, which the superstitious say keeps the meat from running off the spit.

items.name: Borderland Wolf Sausage
items.effect: Lean wolf or worg meat ground with bear fat, salt and pot-herbs, stuffed and cold-smoked over hardwood. A link counts as a day's food and keeps for a week; for 1 hour after eating one you gain +1 on Wisdom (Survival) checks to follow tracks.

recipe.lore: Frontier folk swear the surest way to stop a wolf eating you is to eat it first, and hang the links where the pack can smell them.

items.name: Whaler's Blubber Broth
items.effect: A greasy, scalding broth of rendered blubber and northern meat that sits in the belly like a banked fire. For 8 hours you automatically succeed on saving throws against extreme cold, and a swim in freezing water doesn't cost you a level of exhaustion.

recipe.lore: The blubber is rendered over a slow flame until it stops spitting, and the snowcap berries go in last so their chill locks the warmth inside the belly.

items.name: Echo-Cave Bat-Ear Crisps
items.effect: Paper-thin fried bat ears dusted with shaved truffle and salt. For 8 hours you have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing, and while you are blinded or in total darkness you still know the direction of any creature within 30 feet that isn't moving silently.

components.label: Fresh bat ears (fry within the hour)

recipe.lore: The ears must hit the fat within the hour they're taken, still twitching; fried late, they crisp up deaf.

items.name: Deepdelver's Mushroom Bake
items.effect: A dense, savoury bake of cave truffle and gloomsight caps set with stone milk. For 8 hours you gain darkvision out to 30 feet; if you already have darkvision, its range increases by 30 feet.

recipe.lore: Deep gnome cooks bake it in a covered stone pot with no lantern lit, insisting the caps sulk and lose their virtue if they see light while cooking.

items.name: Houndsnose Brawn
items.effect: A cold, peppery head-cheese of boiled meat and minced hound or wolf snout set in its own jelly, sold by the slice at butchers' stalls. For 8 hours you have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) and Wisdom (Survival) checks that rely on smell, and you can follow a scent trail up to a day old as a bloodhound would.

recipe.lore: Town ratcatchers and thief-takers buy it by the pound; the trick is to mince the snout raw into the cooling jelly, never to boil it.

items.name: Stonewarden's Cockatrice Custard
items.effect: A wobbling, faintly grey honey custard in a hard crust, baked from a cockatrice egg. For 8 hours you have advantage on saving throws against being petrified, and if you are restrained while turning to stone you may repeat the save at the start of each of your turns.

recipe.lore: Hill-temple wardens eat a slice before descending into a basilisk's den, and swear the custard sets harder the closer you carry it to stone.

items.name: Desert Gizzard Pottage
items.effect: A thick grain porridge simmered around a scavenger bird's gizzard and finished with camel fat. For 8 hours you have advantage on saving throws against disease, and you can eat spoiled or tainted (but nonmagical) food and drink without ill effect.

recipe.lore: Desert guides say the vulture eats death and never sickens; the gizzard is scrubbed in salt three times and simmered whole, then sliced into the pot.

items.name: Smuggler's Inkpot Rice
items.effect: Grain cooked black in octopus ink with diced tentacle and sea salt, a dish of harbour back-rooms. For 8 hours you have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made in dim light or darkness.

recipe.lore: Wharf cooks stir the ink in off the heat; boil it and the grain goes grey, and so, they say, does the eater's luck in the shadows.

items.name: Wallcrawler's Clingvine Salad
items.effect: Wilted clingvine tips and bitter greens tossed with ribbons of pickled frog tongue. For 8 hours you have advantage on Strength (Athletics) checks to climb and on checks to keep hold of a rope, ledge or handhold.

recipe.lore: Cat burglars and steeplejacks eat it standing up; the tongue is pickled overnight so it keeps its grip without gluing your teeth together.

items.name: Hearthfest Clover Pie
items.effect: A broad harvest pie of berries and honeycomb with a single four-leaf clover baked into the filling, cut into eight slices. Up to eight creatures who each eat a slice within the same hour can each, once in the next 8 hours, roll a d4 and add it to one ability check they make.

recipe.lore: Village bakers swear the luck spreads only if the pie is cut and shared at one table; whoever finds the clover in their slice pays for the next one.

items.name: Knitbone Marrow Soup
items.effect: A glossy bone broth with a sliver of still-twitching regenerating flesh simmered in it. The first time in the next 8 hours that you are reduced to fewer than half your hit points, you regain hit points equal to 1d6 + your proficiency bonus.

recipe.lore: Camp surgeons keep a severed troll limb in a lidded crock and pare it nightly for the pot; it grows the slice back by morning, which nobody likes to think about.

items.name: Goatherd's Fernleaf Dumplings
items.effect: Steamed goat-meat dumplings wrapped in featherfall fern fronds, so light they seem to lift off the plate. For 8 hours, when you fall you take damage as though the fall were 20 feet shorter, and you have advantage on Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks to keep your footing on narrow or windswept ledges.

recipe.lore: Pass-guides steam them above a pot with the lid weighted down by a stone, because the first batch they ever made floated out into the snow.

items.name: Hellfire Kettle Stew
items.effect: A blistering red stew that makes eaters sweat smoke. For 8 hours you have resistance to fire damage and suffer no ill effects from extreme heat.

recipe.lore: The gland is lanced over the kettle and its oil cooked out for hours behind a wet curtain; cooks who taste too early lose their eyebrows and their sense of taste for a tenday.

items.name: Frost-Hall Feast
items.effect: A northern longhouse feast: a whole roasted haunch glazed with snowcap berries over a frost-lichen bed, carved for six. Up to six creatures who share it within the same hour each gain resistance to cold damage for 8 hours.

recipe.lore: The haunch roasts all day while the hall's doors stand open to the blizzard, and it is carved only once the fire has burned to embers and nobody's breath steams any more.

items.name: Pearl-Diver's Gillweed Soup
items.effect: A cold green soup of gillweed or a great diver's lung, sea salt and shellfish, slurped on the boat before going over the side. For 4 hours you can breathe underwater as well as in air.

recipe.lore: Pearl divers make it with seawater and never let it boil; the first spoonful feels like drowning, and the second like coming home.

items.name: Ironhide Heart Curry
items.effect: A slow, fiery curry of thick-skinned beast and diced heart over mashed oxheart tuber. When you finish a serving, you gain temporary hit points equal to 2d6 + your level, which last for 8 hours.

recipe.lore: Savanna cooks simmer it in a clay pot sealed with dough and break the seal at the table; if the heart has gone soft, the curry was rushed.

items.name: Antivenom Snake Broth
items.effect: A bitter fenland broth of snake meat and a boiled-out venom sac, cut with wyrmbane thistle so the body learns the poison without the bite. For 8 hours you have resistance to poison damage and advantage on saving throws against being poisoned.

recipe.lore: The venom is boiled three times in fresh water and the water thrown out each time; skip the third boil and the broth teaches its lesson the hard way.

items.name: Lorekeeper's Memory Pudding
items.effect: A dark, steamed suet pudding of memory root and wakeful leaf, served to scholars before they open dangerous books. For 8 hours you have resistance to psychic damage and advantage on Intelligence saving throws.

recipe.lore: Library cooks grate the root while reciting the day's date aloud, so the pudding remembers what it is for and doesn't send the eater wandering through old childhood afternoons.
